result.topic_en: Since no general closed-form solution for an arbitrary initial state of the vibrating lamina is available, Euler expands the displacement y as a power series in x with time-dependent coefficients P, Q, R, S, and determines the higher coefficients by comparing the series for the time derivative with the series for the fourth space derivative.
result.transcription:
ius problematis, quae ſcilicet ad ſtatum quemcunque initialem laminae accommodari poſſet, prouti hoc negotium in chordis vibrantibus ſucceſſit, nullo adhuc modo exſpectari poteſt, interim per ſeries infinitas quodammodo hunc defectum ſupplere licet. Denotent enim hae quatuor litterae P, Q, R, S functiones quaſcunque temporis $t$, ac ſtatuatur per ſeriem infinitam:
$y = P + \frac{Qx}{b} + \frac{Rx^2}{b^2} + \frac{Sx^3}{b^3} + \frac{P'x^4}{b^4} + \frac{Q'x^5}{b^5} + \frac{R'x^6}{b^6} + \frac{S'x^7}{b^7}$
$+ \frac{P''x^8}{b^8} + \frac{Q''x^9}{b^9} + \frac{R''x^{10}}{b^{10}} + \frac{S''x^{11}}{b^{11}}$ etc.
hinc colligimus
$-\left(\frac{ddy}{dt^2}\right) = -\frac{ddP}{dt^2} - \frac{x}{b}\cdot\frac{ddQ}{dt^2} - \frac{x^2}{b^2}\frac{ddR}{dt^2} - \frac{x^3}{b^3}\frac{ddS}{dt^2} - \frac{x^4}{b^4}\frac{ddP'}{dt^2} - \frac{x^5}{b^5}\frac{ddQ'}{dt^2}$
$- \frac{x^6}{b^6}\frac{ddR'}{dt^2} - \frac{x^7}{b^7}\frac{ddS'}{dt^2} - \frac{x^8}{b^8}\frac{ddP''}{dt^2} - \frac{x^9}{b^9}\frac{ddQ''}{dt^2} - \frac{x^{10}}{b^{10}}\frac{ddR''}{dt^2}$ etc.
ſimilique modo ſumto tantum $x$ variabili
$b^4\left(\frac{d^4y}{dx^4}\right) = +1.2.3.4\,P' + 2.3.4.5\,Q'\frac{x}{b} + 3.4.5.6\,R'\frac{x^2}{b^2} + 4.5.6.7\,S'\frac{x^3}{b^3}$
$+ 5.6.7.8\,P''\frac{x^4}{b^4} + 6.7.8.9\,Q''\frac{x^5}{b^5} + 7.8.9.10\,R''\frac{b^6}{x^6} + 8.9.10.11\,S''\frac{x^7}{b^7}$ etc.
quae ſeries quum illi aequalis eſſe debeat, ſequentes ſponte ſe produnt determinationes
$P' = -\frac{ddP}{1.2.3.4\,dt^2}$; $Q' = -\frac{ddQ}{2.3.4.5\,dt^2}$; $R' = -\frac{ddR}{3.4.5.6\,dt^2}$
$S' = -\frac{ddS}{4.5.6.7\,dt^2}$; $P'' = -\frac{ddP'}{5.6.7.8\,dt^2}$; $= +\frac{d^4P}{1.2.3.4.5.6.7.8\,dt^2}$
$Q'' = +\frac{d^4Q}{2\ldots\ldots 9\,dt^2}$; $R'' = +\frac{d^4R}{3.4\ldots 10\,dt^2}$; $S'' = \frac{d^4S}{4.5\ldots 11\,dt^2}$ etc.
XII. His determinationibus inuentis, valor applicatae $y$ ex quatuor ſequentibus ſeriebus infinitis reperietur compoſitus:
$y = +$

items.quote: ius problematis, quae ſcilicet ad ſtatum quemcunque initialem laminae accommodari poſſet, prouti hoc negotium in chordis vibrantibus ſucceſſit, nullo adhuc modo exſpectari poteſt
items.english: [a general solution] of this problem, namely one that could be adapted to any initial state of the lamina, as was achieved for vibrating strings, can in no way yet be expected.

items.quote: interim per ſeries infinitas quodammodo hunc defectum ſupplere licet
items.english: Meanwhile, this deficiency may to some extent be made up by means of infinite series.
